query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a single, optimized post‐solidification aging heat treatment to the uniform, fine‐lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will precipitate nano-scale intermetallic particles at the lamellar interfaces, thereby simultaneously enhancing strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance under the extreme service conditions typical of fasteners.
generation.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy that has not undergone any post-solidification aging or secondary phase treatment.
generation.intervention: A heat treatment process consisting of a solutionizing step followed by an aging step. The aging is conducted at an elevated temperature (for example, in the 500–600°C range) for several hours in an inert atmosphere to promote the controlled precipitation of nano-scale intermetallic phases along the lamellar boundaries.
generation.conditions: The heat treatment will be performed in a controlled furnace with an argon atmosphere to prevent oxidation. Subsequent performance testing will simulate service conditions: cyclic temperature fluctuations (e.g. cycling between -40°C and 300°C), long-term mechanical loading including room-temperature creep tests under constant load, and corrosion evaluations using standardized salt spray tests.
generation.structural_mediator: Nano-scale intermetallic precipitates forming at the lamellar interfaces, which increase interfacial cohesion and act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
generation.mechanism: Precipitation hardening: The aging treatment induces the formation of dispersoids that reinforce the lamellar boundaries and impede dislocation motion. This dual strengthening mechanism mitigates creep deformation under long-term loading, while the stabilized interfaces reduce the initiation sites for corrosion and fatigue cracks, thus also enhancing performance during thermal cycling and corrosive exposure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline alloy, the aged alloy is expected to exhibit increased yield and ultimate tensile strength, improved ductility, reduced creep strain (i.e. improved creep resistance), and slower corrosion rates.
generation.baseline: The as-solidified, uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy without any post-solidification aging treatment.
generation.boundary: Improvements are anticipated under conditions typical for fasteners: temperature cycles between about -40°C and 300°C, constant room-temperature load conditions (for creep up to durations relevant for industrial use), and corrosive exposure (e.g., salt spray environments). Performance outside these temperature and loading regimes is not guaranteed.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal aging temperature and duration for precisely controlling precipitate size and distribution have not been determined; there is some risk that overaging or non-uniform precipitation could adversely affect ductility. The quantitative degree of improvement (e.g., percentage increases) is uncertain until experimentally verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples: one group will receive the optimized solutionizing-plus-aging treatment and the other will remain in the as-solidified state. Subject both groups to comprehensive testing including high-cycle tensile tests, room temperature constant-load creep tests, thermal cycling between -40°C and 300°C, and standardized salt spray corrosion tests. Monitor mechanical properties and microstructural evolution via TEM for precipitate verification.
measurements: Tensile properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation)
Creep strain under a defined constant load over a prescribed time
Thermal cycling life (number of cycles until crack initiation or failure)
Corrosion rate (via weight loss or electrochemical impedance spectroscopy)
Microstructural analysis (TEM imaging to confirm the presence and distribution of nano-scale precipitates)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged (treated) samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements—defined here as at least a 10% increase in strength and ductility, a measureable reduction (≥10%) in creep strain under equivalent loading, and demonstrably improved corrosion resistance (lower corrosion rates) compared to the as-solidified baseline—the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
